abstract.para: A reproducible build is a software engineering practice guaranteeing that compiling the exact same source code in the exact same environment always produces binary identical executables, distribution packages or filesystem images.

section.title: What is a reproducible build?
section.para: A reproducible build is a software engineering practice guaranteeing that compiling the exact same source code in the exact same environment always produces binary identical executables, distribution packages or filesystem images. The same environment means: dependencies and their versions, build configuration flags and environment variables as far as they are used by the build system.
If you compile the source code, the resulting checksum must perfectly match the checksum of the officially distributed release.

section.title: Why are reproducible builds important?
section.para: In standard pipelines, identical source code can produce slightly different binaries each time it is compiled. While functionally identical, these arbitrary differences make it impossible to prove that a binary was generated exclusively from the trusted source code. Reproducible builds solve this by creating a verifiable chain of trust.

formalpara.title: Supply chain security
formalpara.para: If a build server is compromised and malicious code is injected during compilation, the resulting binary will yield a different checksum than a clean, locally compiled version. This prevents attacks where the source code repository appears safe but the distributed binary is secretly backdoored.

formalpara.title: Debugging simplification
formalpara.para: Eliminating build variance removes a major variable when troubleshooting environmental problems.
